data.narrative:
Captura is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Harry Atwater and CX Xiang that has raised $30M+ to date. The valuation landscape for frontier climate tech includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers spanning battery materials, hydrogen, and metals recycling—though direct same-stage comparables within this cohort remain limited.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable framework here. Using total capital raised ($30M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $60M. The peer-median approach is not reliable in this instance; while eight same-sector private companies exist, none of the targeted filters—identical stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier—yielded the three or more datapoints required for robust median analysis. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to one applicable method, supports a valuation range of $51M (low) to $69M (high) with a median of $60M. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficiently dense peer data at Captura's specific stage and valuation tier, limiting confidence in any single-method conclusion. Near-term funding events or updated financials from existing Climate & Energy comparables would strengthen conviction in this range.
